title: Asking pardon to list vices matched to virtues
english: I hold it necessary to lay out briefly for your love of labor the vices paired against the virtues. Up to this point we have plowed the mind and thrown up the thorns of our thoughts out of the sown land. We have not come this far by works we ourselves have done. We hold a pattern of sound words we heard from the Fathers, and we have become witnesses to some of their practices.

The whole work is grace from above. Grace shows even to sinners the plots of the mind deceivers, and it guards us and speaks, saying, "What do you have that you did not receive?" (1 Corinthians 4:7) It does this so that in receiving we may give thanks to the Giver, instead of assigning to ourselves any boast of glory by denying the gift. So grace says, "If you did receive it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?" (1 Corinthians 4:7) "You have already become rich," grace says (1 Corinthians 4:8) — you who are poor in works — "you have already had your fill," you who have only begun to be taught — whose delusion has just now passed over into me. Through it I have borrowed a reckoning that hides my poverty in works, and through the counsel I urged I have turned the learner's place of being taught on its head.

Still, if you keep any pardon in reserve, grant it to me as well, so that I may lay out briefly the vices paired against the virtues and show what each is: what gluttony is, and self-control set against it; what sexual immorality is, and chastity; what love of money is, and poverty; grief, and joy set against it; what anger is, and patience; listlessness, and endurance; what vainglory is, and freedom from vainglory; envy, and freedom from envy; pride, and humility. These stand paired against one another, contending and set over against one another, and in this brief form I have laid them out.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

orientation: Evagrius opens by saying his teaching comes from grace and the Fathers, and he asks pardon before listing the vices paired with their virtues.
